name: Willis L. Eaton
role: Stockman, one of the Eaton brothers; Billings County assessor
bio: Willis L. Eaton was a Little Missouri stockman and an active member of the Little Missouri River Stockgrowers' Association, making motions at its meetings in 1885 and 1886. He spent the winter of 1884-85 visiting his sister in Pittsburgh and in October 1885 was a pallbearer at a ranch funeral. He was elected Billings County assessor in April 1886 and spent the spring and early summer assessing a territory the paper put at about 200 by 50 miles, finishing by July 1. At the August 1886 stockmen's meeting he moved on the back taxes paid by the railroad on behalf of Billings County, and he was re-elected assessor in November 1886.
